malformed_rows.description: Rows without a problem statement or gold context.
malformed_rows.adapter_handling: corrections.json restores a missing problem statement from the source release the row copies, and the generation report lists the restoration. A row that cannot be restored aborts generation when it is selected; with --skip-invalid-source-rows it is skipped, and the generation report lists it either way.
malformed_rows.not_restorable: Gold context is ContextBench's own annotation, and no source benchmark has it. These rows' gold context is empty in every published ContextBench revision: the pinned commit, which is still the latest on GitHub, and every revision of the Hugging Face dataset Contextbench/ContextBench.

full.error: gold_context must be a non-empty list
gold_context must be a non-empty list
gold_context must be a non-empty list

truncated_repo_column.description: Multi-SWE-bench rows whose `repo` column is cut at the first hyphen of the repository name, for example fasterxml/jackson for fasterxml/jackson-core.
truncated_repo_column.adapter_handling: The adapter ignores `repo`. It takes the repository from `repo_url`, else from `original_inst_id`, and rejects rows where the two disagree.

split_disagrees_with_verified.description: `verified` is the union of the two splits and a subset of `full`, but the rows for one instance are not always equal. Rows are compared with `verified` on their shared columns.
split_disagrees_with_verified.adapter_handling: Each dataset keeps its own content, and every task name includes the dataset, so one task name never maps to two contents.

unmatchable_gold_files.description: Gold files, as the verifier scores them, that no prediction can match, so they cap the oracle's file coverage at `oracle_maximum`. `gold_path_mangled_upstream`: the annotation names an existing dotfile by a repository-relative path, and ContextBench's gold parser strips the dot with `lstrip("./")`, so `.github/x.yml` is scored as `github/x.yml`. `absent_at_base_commit`: the file does not exist at the base commit, such as a reproduction script the annotator wrote.
unmatchable_gold_files.adapter_handling: Kept, as in native scoring: gold.json keeps the raw paths, and the verifier normalizes them once with ContextBench's parser, so these tasks cannot reach a reward of 1.0.

gold_ranges_past_eof.description: Gold ranges that end past the end of the file at the base commit, most by one line.
gold_ranges_past_eof.adapter_handling: The verifier clamps a read's declared range to the base file and drops a range that starts past its end (ATTRIBUTION.md), so the oracle's reads of these files are credited.

wrong_problem_statements.description: Rows whose problem statement describes a different change than the instance's gold patch. Each family's statements were compared with the source release they copy, and SWE-bench Pro statements also with the requirements and interface that release gives for the same instance.
wrong_problem_statements.adapter_handling: Corrected at generation from corrections.json, which names the source and revision of each corrected value; the generation report lists every applied correction.

not_checked.Multi: Multi-SWE-bench's dataset is 1.5 GB of JSONL

pro_requirements_check.verdict: kept: the statement is the BSD uptime issue that the patch fixes, and SWE-bench Pro v1's requirements ask for an uptime_seconds fact on BSD hosts

json_quoted_problem_statements.description: Problem statements stored as a JSON string literal, so the text shows its quotes and \n escapes. The source release stores them the same way; SWE-bench Pro V2 stores none of them quoted.
json_quoted_problem_statements.adapter_handling: Decoded at generation when the whole value is one JSON string literal (adapter.decoded_json_string); the generation report lists the decoded rows. A corrected statement is replaced instead.

polybench_untracked_dockerfile.description: SWE-PolyBench builds each image by copying the build context into /testbed (`WORKDIR /testbed`, `COPY . .`), so the checkout holds the Dockerfile the image was built from as an untracked /testbed/Dockerfile.
polybench_untracked_dockerfile.adapter_handling: Left out of the model patch. ContextBench's OpenHands runner exports with `git add -A` and `git diff --cached <base>`, so its patches add Dockerfile; the agent image lists the image's untracked files in .git/info/exclude, so the adapter's patches do not. Edit localization counts only deleted lines, so the added file changes no metric. Where the repository tracks a root Dockerfile (`tracked_dockerfile_overwritten`), the image overwrote it. The agent image keeps the overwritten file, as native agents see it, and records it in the model patch's baseline. Upstream's patch would then modify Dockerfile, and its deleted lines would count as edits outside the gold context; the adapter's does not.
